title: Reverse Win
summary: Work backward from the mating square to force the rook through the wrong defensive line.

nodes.question: How can the bishop reach a3 without allowing ...Rb7?
nodes.explanation: White has Kc1, Be7 and c2 against Ka1, Rf7, Bd1 and a2. Be7 must draw the rook off the seventh rank before choosing the a3 diagonal.

branches.title: Force the rook away from the seventh rank
commentary: Begin from the complete seven-piece source root. Each bishop move creates a different mating threat and forces the rook to change its defensive geometry.
Bd6 threatens Be5 mate along the e5–a1 diagonal.
Rf5 blocks that threat along the fifth rank, preparing to meet Be5 with ...Rxe5.
Bb4 switches the threat to Bc3 mate.
Rf3 guards c3 from the third rank.
Bc5 switches to Bd4 mate.
Rf4 guards d4 from the fourth rank, finally leaving the rook unable to return to b7 in one move.
Ba3 now threatens Bb2 mate. From f4 the rook cannot block the b-file with ...Rb7.
Bxc2 captures White’s last pawn in the illustrated source reply, but it does not stop the mate.
Bb2# is actual mate. Kc1 protects b2 and covers b1, while Black’s own a2 pawn closes a2.
branches.explanation: Bb2# is actual mate. Kc1 protects b2 and covers b1, while Black’s own a2 pawn closes a2.

branches.title: Try the final diagonal immediately
commentary: Compare the source’s initial attempt to use the desired a3 diagonal before diverting the rook.
Ba3 threatens Bb2 mate but leaves the rook able to use the seventh rank.
Rb7 gets behind b2 along the b-file.
Bb2+ checks, but the bishop can now be captured.
Rxb2 removes the bishop and stops the mating plan. This exact comparison’s outcome is checked rather than inferred from material. The exact remaining position is winning for Black.
branches.explanation: Rxb2 removes the bishop and stops the mating plan. This exact comparison’s outcome is checked rather than inferred from material. The exact remaining position is winning for Black.

branches.title: Skip the first forcing bishop move
commentary: Compare moving to b4 before forcing the rook down the f-file.
Bb4 threatens Bc3 mate, but the rook is still free to defend from the seventh rank.
Rc7 prepares to meet Bc3 down the c-file.
Bc5 offers the bishop on the rook’s file without the intended f3 geometry.
Rxc5 removes the bishop. This independently supplied capture tests the concrete consequence of the premature move order. The exact remaining position is winning for Black.

branches.explanation: Rxc5 removes the bishop. This independently supplied capture tests the concrete consequence of the premature move order. The exact remaining position is winning for Black.

exercises.prompt: Why start with Bd6 instead of Ba3?
exercises.answer: Bd6 forces ...Rf5; Bb4 then draws the rook to f3, and Bc5 to f4. Only then does Ba3 leave the rook unable to reach b7 in one move.

startContext: Begin from the complete seven-piece source root at zero seconds. The full Bd6–Bb4–Bc5–Ba3 maneuver and selected premature attempts are checked. The premature b4 capture completion is independently supplied.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
